entries.summary: Open Setup with function two, then choose Backup. The backup is encrypted. Keep its key, snapshot and deletion proof.
steps: Plug in a backup drive and choose it in Backup.
Keep the encryption key apart from the backup. Anyone with both can read what was saved.
Write down the checkpoint shown on screen. A full restore uses it to verify the deletion proof.

entries.summary: Boot from a PipOS Try stick and choose Restore a being. Restoring is an installation and erases the target disk.
steps: For a full restore, bring the snapshot, key, deletion proof and the checkpoint you recorded.
Choose the intended internal disk, inspect what will be erased and follow the typed confirmation on screen.

entries.summary: Function nine recovers the face when the lid reading is unknown. On the MacBook, hold the function key while pressing F nine.
Open the Quick Menu with function six, or say open the Quick Menu. Use the arrow keys and Enter to select an app. Escape closes it.
Function two or Mission Control opens Setup on an installed Pip. In Try, it opens the start menu.
Function one toggles captions. Captions start off. The screen clears private caption text when a guest arrives.
Function ten toggles my microphone. On the MacBook, the printed speaker mute key controls the speaker. Hold function to use microphone mute.
Say start guest mode for a private conversation, and end guest mode when it is over. Saved memory and personal screen apps stay closed to guests.
Say you can use your camera and press E at the screen to allow it. Say stop watching to turn permission off.
Say you can dream tonight. Check the date on screen and press Y for that one night. Say stop dreaming to switch it off.
Boot from the Try stick first. The installer shows the disks and their contents, then asks for typed confirmation before erasing the target.
steps: Back up anything you need from the target disk before starting.
Open the installer from the Try menu and check the capacity and partitions on the disk it offers.
If power fails before the installer finishes, boot from the USB and start the installation again.

entries.summary: Say open the terminal. When I write a command or script for you, check what I show and say run it when ready.
Ask me to forget a topic or a day. I'll tell you what I found and wait for yes before deleting it.
steps: For just the memory I last read back, say forget that.
After a deletion, export an updated deletion proof to keep the memory gone when you restore a backup.

entries.summary: Say set a timer for five minutes, or name another duration. Ask how long left on my timer, or say cancel the timer.
Say set an alarm for 6:30 tomorrow, or set an alarm for ten minutes. Alarms can ring during quiet hours.
Give the task and time together, for example remind me to close the window tomorrow at nine a.m. Ask what are my reminders to hear pending items.
Open Setup, then choose Quiet hours and announcements. During quiet hours, automatic reminders and timers wait. Alarms can still ring.
Say add milk to my shopping list, or ask what's on my shopping list. Say cross off milk when you have it.
Say make a note, followed by what to keep. Say read my notes to hear the saved notes. For the most recent note, you can say delete my last note.
After a topic, say pick this up later. Ask what were we working on to bring it back. Say close the thread to remove the bookmark.
Say open the calculator or choose Calculator in the Quick Menu. You can also say an arithmetic question directly, such as what's fifteen times eight.
Choose Time zone in Setup, or say set my time zone to Australia Sydney for that example. Use an exact region and city when the zone name needs both.
On an installed system with Internet mode and web lookups allowed, ask for the weather and give a city if one isn't saved. You can ask about today or tomorrow.
